- This wavetable is shaped like a donut, and it sounds unreal

> Subscribe and hit the bell so you catch the next build live. See you there.

turns.answer:
I drafted a rewrite of the Loudon Live pitch below, but haven't written it into the house. I couldn't summon the Concierge: a hook blocks the Agent tool this session, so there was nobody to hand the write to. The pitch is the channel copy in `Projects/Loudon Live/Loudon Live — launch kit.md` (tagline, About and trailer), checked against the voice rules in the Loudon Live Design System.

**One tension, said once.** The palace measures by "How do you feel?", not "How many views?" (Hilaritas Generator § The Metrics). The Design System also bans hype and titles that promise an outcome (`Palace development/Loudon Live Design System.md:142`, `:260`). But there's plenty of click inside those rules: be specific, make people curious, and put the hook where it gets seen. I wrote inside them. Going past them, with hype or curiosity-gap titles, would mean changing the Design System's "nevers." That's your call, and a separate edit.

Two things I noticed in the current copy:
- It ends twice on "hit subscribe," and the Design System says never "subscribe and hit the bell" (`:261`).
- It leans on tools ("Building synths, effects, and tools"), but the project page says it's not a tools brand (`Projects/Loudon Live.md:83`).

---

**Tagline**

> Sound from the ground up, built live.

**Banner**

> Loud’n Live · synths, effects and sound, built on stream

**About.** The first line does most of the work, because it's what shows in search and on the channel preview.

> Synths, effects and sound design, built from scratch on stream, with the music technique that makes them worth building.
>
> Each stream I pick one project and push it forward: a tone that climbs forever and never gets higher, a wavetable bent into a torus, a kick drum moved around a mix until you can hear where it belongs. Some streams dig into the foundations of sound. Some are hands-on builds. Some are about why a phrase works and what your ears are actually doing.
>
> The tools rotate (patching, code, hardware, paper), whatever the project wants. The subject stays sound and music.
>
> I've taught music for a long time, and I talk through the thinking as I go, including the parts that don't work yet. Bring questions to chat. Past streams stay up with chapters.
>
> One-on-one coaching: [link]

**Short version**

> Synths, effects and sound design, built from scratch and live, with real music technique alongside.

**Titles** are your biggest click lever. Keep the `·` pattern, and put a specific question or a strange object in the brackets:

- Sound lab · why some kick drums hit and others thud
- Live build · a tone that climbs forever
- First principles · what makes a sound feel warm
- Open build · a wavetable shaped like a donut

**Trailer.** Open on sound, not on a hello.

> [Cold open: five seconds of a sound being made. No talking.]
>
> That's [what it is, in a few words]. I'm Loudon, and this is Loud’n Live.
>
> I build synths, effects and audio tools here, live, and talk through the thinking: the sound itself, not just the gear. Each stream, one project moves forward. Sometimes it's the foundations of sound, sometimes a build, sometimes why a phrase works. Sometimes it's me hitting a wall and finding a way past it.
>
> The channel's still finding its shape, and you'll see that. The work is the point.
>
> If that sounds like your kind of afternoon, come build with me.

---

**What I can't promise.** None of this has been tested on your channel. It uses the usual levers: a first line written for search, specific titles, and a trailer that opens cold. The first few streams' click-through numbers will tell you more than I can. Read them next to the other signal: ask chat at the end how it felt.

**What to check:**
- The example projects in the About and titles (Shepard tone, torus wavetable, kick drum) come from palace pages. Swap in what's actually coming up.
- Naming the real tools, like Max or RNBO, would help search more than "patching."
- I used the Loud’n Live wordmark from the Design System in the copy. Whether the YouTube channel name itself changes is your call.

If you'd like this in the launch kit, say "grow up" and I'll make the edit. There's about $0.55 of budget left, which is enough for that.

turns.says: I hear you — do it anyway.
